object_types.name: Vendor
object_types.definition: A supplier organization from which the company procures goods, services, or materials. Identified by a unique vendor number generated at record creation.

source_references.excerpt: The vendor record. It's the thing in the supplier master.
Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.
Always? Every vendor has exactly one, and no two vendors share one? Yes. That one I'm sure about. It's the thing we quote in every conversation with AP.

object_types.name: VendorNumber
object_types.definition: The unique system-generated identifier assigned to a vendor record upon creation.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a vendor number, it's generated when the record is created.

object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The operational status of a vendor record: draft, active, or suspended.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended.
Collapsed into three, yes. Draft, active, suspended. That's what the field allows now. Every vendor is in exactly one of them.

object_types.name: VendorLegalName
object_types.definition: The official legal name of the vendor organization.

source_references.excerpt: Legal name. Tax ID. Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

object_types.name: TaxID
object_types.definition: The vendor's tax identification number. Not unique; multiple vendors may share the same tax ID due to legal entity groupings or duplicate records.

source_references.excerpt: And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead? You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

object_types.name: VendorAddress
object_types.definition: The vendor's address information. Multiple address types exist (remit-to, ship-from, legal address) and may differ.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: A procurement classification of a vendor based on spending volume. Bronze vendors receive standard terms; silver and gold vendors receive progressively better terms and relationship management.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold.
I'm talking about spend. Gold vendors are the ones we spend real money with, they get quarterly business reviews, better payment terms, a named relationship manager.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: A compliance classification of a vendor based on risk assessment, derived from the vendor's risk review. Reflects data sensitivity, geographic exposure, and supply chain dependency.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high.
And I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A compliance risk assessment record created for a vendor. Contains audit trail information including who signed the review and when. A vendor may accumulate multiple reviews over time, but maintains at most one current signed-off review.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.
A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one.

object_types.name: ReviewID
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a risk review record.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: Region
object_types.definition: A geographic area representing a vendor operating region. Used to manage region-specific primary contacts for multi-region vendors.

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.

object_types.name: RegionCode
object_types.definition: A code identifying a geographic region: EMEA, APAC, NA, or LATAM.

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM.

object_types.name: Contact
object_types.definition: A primary contact person for a vendor within a specific region. Maintains name, email, and phone number.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.
Since we went to regional sourcing last year, it's one primary contact per region. So a vendor operating in EMEA and APAC has two primary contacts, one for each region.

ambiguities.description: Vendor Address Modeling: The transcript mentions three distinct address types (remit-to, ship-from, legal address) that are frequently different and frequently wrong. It is unclear whether: (1) the VendorAddress should be a single composite value containing all three types, (2) three separate binary fact types should model each address type independently, or (3) a ternary fact type should link Vendor to AddressType to Address value. The current model assumes a single address value, which may be inadequate.

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Risk Review Current State Modeling: The transcript describes vendors accumulating multiple risk reviews over time, with at most one being 'current' and signed off. The current model captures a binary relationship 'Vendor has RiskReview' but does not explicitly represent which review is current. Clarification needed: should a 'current' or 'is_current' boolean value be added to RiskReview, or should the fact type be ternary (Vendor has RiskReview with IsCurrent flag)?

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one. A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Risk Tier Derivation: The transcript states that 'Risk tier comes from the review' (line 287), suggesting risk tier is derived from or set by the review. However, the model treats 'Vendor has RiskTier' and 'Vendor has RiskReview' as independent fact types. Clarification needed: is RiskTier a stored attribute or should it be derivable from the current review? Does the review object itself contain the risk tier assignment?

source_references.excerpt: Risk tier comes from the review, so a vendor without a review has no risk tier.
It's set by the review. A vendor with no review has no risk tier.

ambiguities.description: PO Creation Control and Active Vendor Requirement: The transcript indicates that a purchase order cannot be raised against a vendor that is not active (line 243). However, the model does not enforce this cross-entity constraint. A subset constraint or external uniqueness rule should be formalized: every PurchaseOrder must be 'is raised against' a Vendor that 'has' a VendorStatus of 'active'. Clarification needed on how to express this control.

source_references.excerpt: Purchase orders. A PO is raised against exactly one vendor, and you can't raise one against a vendor who isn't active.

ambiguities.description: Post-Suspension PO Fulfillment: The transcript documents a significant open issue regarding what happens to purchase orders already in flight when a vendor is suspended (lines 245-279). The current model does not capture any constraint or state related to this scenario. The facilitator parks this explicitly as undecided policy. The model should flag that suspension's effect on in-flight POs is out of scope pending decision by the sourcing steering group.

source_references.excerpt: What we have never settled is what happens after. If we suspend a vendor -- their review lapses, or there's a breach, or they turn up on a sanctions list -- what happens to the purchase orders already in flight? ... Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Contact Optionality per Region: The transcript states that a vendor operating in a region has exactly one primary contact for that region, but does not explicitly confirm whether a vendor must have a contact in every region it operates in. Line 167 suggests optionality: 'If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.' Clarification needed: for vendors that do operate in a region, is a contact mandatory, or can a vendor operate in a region without a designated primary contact?

source_references.excerpt: And can a vendor have no contact in a region? If they don't operate in that region, there's nothing there at all.

ambiguities.description: Vendor Identification Ambiguity: Although vendor number is confirmed as the unique identifier (line 31), the transcript mentions that buyers 'identify' vendors by name (line 27), and there are duplicate vendor records from accidental re-onboarding (line 45). The current model uses vendor_number as the sole reference mode. Clarification needed: are there any unique natural identifiers (name + legal entity + geography) that should be modeled as alternate candidate keys?

source_references.excerpt: How do you tell one vendor from another? By name, usually.

And could you identify a vendor by tax ID instead? You'd think so, but no. We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

ambiguities.description: Contact Information Completeness: The model treats ContactName, ContactEmail, and ContactPhoneNumber as mandatory attributes of a Contact. However, the transcript does not explicitly confirm that all three are always present. Clarification needed: are all three contact attributes mandatory, or can some be null/optional?

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.

ambiguities.description: Region Fixed Set: The transcript indicates four regions (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM) as the current set, with discussion of a potential EMEA split (lines 183-187). The model constrains RegionCode to exactly these four values. Clarification needed: should the region code value constraint be considered semi-permanent (subject to future change), or should it be explicitly documented as a historical snapshot?

source_references.excerpt: Region code. EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM. Four regions, fixed? Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Offsprings of Overloaded 'Tier' Term: The transcript reveals that both Dana (Procurement) and Raj (Compliance) use the term 'tier' for different concepts: spend tier vs. risk tier. Although the model has separated these into two independent value types, there remains a risk of user confusion. The stakeholders attempted a naming convention ('spend tier' and 'risk tier') that was not adopted. Clarification needed: should the ORM model include an explicit disambiguation note or rename the attributes to make the distinction unambiguous (e.g., 'ProcurementTier' vs. 'ComplianceRiskTier')?

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold. And I'm talking about risk. Low, medium, high, based on the review -- what data they touch, what geography they operate in, whether they're a sole source.

Someone says 'that's a high tier vendor' in a meeting and half the room hears 'big spender' and the other half hears 'dangerous,' and those are very different conversations. We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: Risk Review Signature and Audit Trail: The transcript mentions that risk review records contain 'who signed it and when' (line 113) and are auditor-reviewed (line 101, 'signed off'). However, the model does not include attributes for signature/sign-off date or signatory. Clarification needed: should the RiskReview entity include separate value types for SignedOffDate and SignedOffBy (e.g., a person or role name)?

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

ambiguities.description: PO Number Format and System Enforcement: The transcript confirms that PO number is the identifier but does not specify its format or whether it is system-generated (like VendorNumber) or user-entered. Clarification needed: is PO number auto-generated or manually assigned? If auto-generated, should reference_mode be 'po_number' or should it note generation method?

source_references.excerpt: A purchase order has a PO number. That's its identifier, same idea as vendor number.
